channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [6] Staging and defect-limited intercalation of FeCl3 in graphite electrodes
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Colin Ophus, Andrew M. Minor

Authors: Peter Schweizer, Lilian M. Vogl, Colin Ophus, Andrew M. Minor

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Study of intercalation in graphite, relevant to tuning 2D materials and vdW heterostructures.

Tags: #material #graphite #microscopy

Abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 16 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74399-w Using transmission electron microscopy, this study reveals the 3D structure of partially intercalated graphite, showing breakdowns in conventional staging behavior and highlighting how lattice defects govern early-stage intercalation.
